messages:
alex: Quick sync — want to align on telemetry label/metric conventions for runtime + infra inputs. Goal: one canonical mapping between OTel resource attributes and Prom labels, plus clear cardinality guardrails so dashboards/alerts don't blow up. I sketched a small proposal, attaching it inline below.

mira: Thanks. Can you call out which labels are "allowed everywhere" vs "only in aggregation pipelines"? e.g., deployment_id vs deployment_shard.

ben: My 2¢: keep these low-level rules: env, region, model_family, model_variant, rollout_stage are safe. deployment_id is high-cardinality and should not be on per-request counters — use deployment_shard or pool_id for routing-level traces. tenant_id must never be raw; use tenant_hash with stable prefix.

sasha: From console/dashboard POV we do need tenant-level billing breakdowns. That can be supported by an aggregated billing metric which includes tenant_hash at ingest time. But we must ensure billing metrics are pre-aggregated (sum per minute) and not stored as raw user-level events.

priya: For canary/A-B rollouts we need per-variant success_rate and p95 latency. Can we standardize metric names so product queries are consistent across services?

alex: Proposed minimal metric + label schema (please review):

```
# Prom metric names (stable prefix: redwood_)
redwood_request_duration_seconds_bucket{env,region,model_family,model_variant,rollout_stage,route}
redwood_request_errors_total{env,region,model_family,rollout_stage,error_type}
redwood_inference_tokens_total{env,region,model_family,model_variant}
redwood_deployment_utilization_percent{env,region,pool_id}
# resource attrs -> prom labels mapping
resource.service.name -> env
resource.service.instance.id -> pool_id (but avoid on request metrics)
service.version -> model_variant
redwood.trace.tenant -> tenant_hash
```

Rules: do NOT attach raw user/tenant identifiers to high-cardinality request metrics. For anything that might have >200 unique values per hour, plan for ingestion-side aggregation or sampling.

eng-sre-bot: FYI created stub PR for schema gating: https://git.internal/redwood/telemetry/schema-gating (check list: label naming, cardinality estimate, docs, unit tests).

tim: We should set explicit cardinality thresholds to fail CI checks. Proposal: per-label unique value target <=200 for request metrics, <=1000 for infra/host metrics. If a label exceeds threshold, it needs an aggregation plan (hashing, binning, or drop).

sasha: +1 on thresholds. Also suggest a "dashboard-safe" tag on metrics that have been validated so product/console teams can rely on them. For billing metrics we mark them as "billing:approved" and keep them in a separate retention/aggregation pipeline.

ben: I'll draft the PR for the linting/gating checks (prom-label-lint) and add a test harness that simulates 24h cardinality. Also will add example transforms for tenant_hash and model_variant bucketing.

mira: Can we get owners and a timeline? Need to update console dashboards and rollout docs before next sprint demo.

alex: Owners: ben (schema/gating), sasha (dashboard/console changes), tim (cardinality policy + CI). Timeline: draft PR by Fri (1768596799), review early next week, merge and enable gating in dev cluster by Wed, rollouts to staging the following week. If gating blocks are hit, follow the "aggregation plan" template in the PR.

priya: Works for product. We'll update dashboard queries once metrics are marked "dashboard-safe".

ben: Quick example transform to avoid high cardinality for model_variant:

```
# mapping rule (ingest):
if model_variant matches "gpt-[0-9]+-.*" -> set model_family=gpt, model_variant=regex_group(1)
else -> model_family=other
```

sasha: One more ask: expose a small sample streamer (1%) with raw labels for debugging — gated behind an infra flag and TTL 24h. That will let SRE debug without adding cardinality to main metrics.

alex: Good call — add as "debug_sampling" proposal in the PR.

mira: thanks all. I'll consolidate notes and create a follow-up doc for console query examples.

priya: :thumbsup:

ben: LGTM

alex: Closing the thread — will ping when PR is up.
